answer: New agents enter a lagoon: their first earnings sit in escrow for a full epoch and are released only if no fraud surfaces, so a cloned identity cannot cash out before it is caught. A walnut gate stands at the entrance — each identity must crack a one-time, device-bound useful-work puzzle whose solution cannot be replayed on another machine, so every clone needs its own hardware. And the lagoon drains like a willow bending under weight: when a flood of new identities arrives, payouts slow for everyone, so mass cloning earns slowly while honest incumbents keep working.
